items.subject: Give it everything you've got
items.summary: Sister Heintzelman shares her busy mission week, including a baptism, and says her mission is ending soon.
items.body:
Apparently when you try to avoid talking or thinking about your mission
ending, everyone else gets the exact opposite idea. Every member and
missionary that I know has been asking me about going home and my last
meals. For some strange reason it feel a like I'm on death row and they are
trying to feed me well before I die.

 Speaking of which we had a very busy week. So let's hit the highlights.

🌟 A very sweet and tender talk with Hermana Pineda

🌟 Spanish exchange with Sister McDonald in La Joya! We got chased by many
dogs, had a cool lesson, and did lots of finding. So my Spanish got some
practice. And the friend we taught Cesar got baptized on Sunday!!!

🌟 We had an awesome lesson with Gabriel, Neydy, and two of their kids. We
hope that they will get to church soon!

🌟 Brenda has been reading her Book of Mormon. There is a lot going on in
her life and some opposition, please pray for her.

🌟 Lessons with Anika, Cesar, and Jesus are my favorite. They are all so
special and loving in such individual and unique ways. So trips to their
different cities are always a blast.

🌟 We had the funniest lesson with Cesar about the word of wisdom. Which
included many pictures, charades, and lots of trips to the kitchen for
Cesar. Buddy literally kept bringing us things to ask if they are good for
you or not. But apparently he is not a fan of eggs but loves to eat cows.

🌟 We finally got to have a lesson with some members of the Cano family.
They are all fluent signers because half of them are deaf and a few are
members. But a bunch of the family moved here recently and so we've been
trying to contact and teach them for awhile. God is so good for opening
that door for us.

 Hardest point of this week was when our dear friend Maria decided she
would no longer come to church or be baptized. I am so grateful to have
been part of her story and I have learned much from teaching her. And I
know that God is also looking out for her and slowly guiding her home.

 All in all this week has been full of love, laughter, and growth. And
the good thing is that we are not slowing down. I'm giving it everything
I've got and laying it all out on the field. And the Lord is spreading His
gospel, we are so lucky to be part of it.

 I want you all to know that God can make the most beautiful garden out
of your worst desert. When you feel like there is nothing around you, know
that God is planting and watering the very ground that you are standing on.
As I have come to these last weeks I keep thinking if I can just help one
more person, do one more thing, teach one more lesson. But the truth is
every single act of kindness and love that you place in this world is a
seed being dropped in the ground. Another sprinkle of water over them as
they grow. The joy comes in doing the work not in seeing the results.
Because I hope that you and I will wake up with that mentality, to reach
out one more time, lift one more heavy heart, dry one more tear. To never
lose the motivation and kindness that this world so desperately needs. For
as Moroni says, "after the trial of your faith" is when the blessings come.
Trust Him, His plan and timing.

 May God be with you all til we meet again.

- Sister Heintzelman 🤟🏼

Also if you want the information for my arrival and my homecoming, God
ahead and reach out!

And check out the flicks:
https://photos.app.goo.gl/BL2FkhmWZah8M4Ut8

(My favorite bench in Brownsville)

(Sister Clifton is a master driver!)

(Love the murals of Brownsville)

(Teaching Cesar the word of wisdom)

items.subject: Great and dreadful day pt2
items.summary: Brysen Schmidt writes from Africa about staying with his companion, moving apartments, and a spiritual thought.
items.body:
Hey everyone hows life going? The work of tye lord is still booming fkr me
down here in africa

I lowkey think im developing alzheimers cause I feel like stuff happened
this week but I cant remember anything. For now, let's talk about transfers

So i am staying in the same area with the same companion, which i am very
much not mad at all about. Here's where things get interesting

I am moving apartments😢. When I heard i was in the celestial apartment,
and usually things stay the same fkr a good 4-6 transfers i was rather
happy. Why is this the celestial apartment you may ask? Because there is
minimal cockroaches (i only see 5-10 a day) and no mice. My next home is an
apartment that the church just bought, so who knows what its gonna be like.
And since I don't have official transfer news yet (the ap and office elders
told me that info) idk who my new roomates will be which jd also sad cause
I like my current gang

Oh well. In terms of african missions apparently ive had it pretty easy, so
ig its time to start getting the real mission experience

Spiritual thought:

On tuesday we had the opportunity to hear a devotional from Elder Morrison
of the 70. He began his message by talking about testimonies. Talking about
how if we are not actively working to grow or protect them how the devil
will begin to break them. It reminded me a lot of Elder Browns talk frkm
October 2025 conference. He talked about how when we finish our mission it
is important that we continue to keep and build what we gained here. Thats
got me thinking, as important as those spiritual experiences are that build
your testimony, its almost more important what happens after. Do you allow
yourself to become better because kf it or allow yourself to go back tk how
you were before? Yes this mission is very important, but what haplens jn
the next few years after is at least of equal importance so I maintain what
I gained these next 2 years.

So when you have a testimony building experience, make sure you continue to
maintain and build what you gained, otherwise it will have been for nothing

Love yall and have a great week!

items.subject: Yup Thats Mamalodi
items.summary: Austin Nelson shares a mission week in Mamelodi with zone leader exchanges and eight investigators at church.
items.body:
Matthew 10:38, 39. -And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after
me, is not worthy of me.He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that
loseth his life for my sake shall find it.

This week Wednesday we went on zone leader exchanges. It was priceless to
see our beloved zone leader walk through Mamelodi. He did not feel
comfortable. We went to a lesson in an informal settlement. You could tell
he was uneasy. When we showed up to meet the guy(Sam), the water turned on.
He said it was a miracle and we were sent from God.

This week was an amzing week for sharing the gospel. We had 8 investors
show up to church which was amazing one of which was Sam! Durring Elders
Quorm the brother giving the lesson wrote the word patience in big letters
on the board
. He asked us all ways in which we could be patient. After there was a
handful of responses he moved the lesson to the next part. He asked "who
all read the conference talk sent on the group chat?" Nobody. Seriously
Nobody raised there hand. His patience imidiately went out the window. He
asked extreamely loudly why we all even come to church if we dont live the
gospel through the week. Everyone in the room just pointing at the big word
on the wall "Patience." Sam our investigator thought it was so funny. He
said next week he would bring his family to church.

The craziest thing that happened this week was guy fox day. It is huge in
Mamelodi. If you want to know what that is you probably dont.

Going to the zoo with my district!!

Google Photos!
https://photos.app.goo.gl/KMnyDCTD9hAvMVs56

Love yall,
Elder Nelson

items.subject: Transfer 3!!
items.summary: Elder McKay Andersen shares his transfer news and a story about inviting a woman to be baptized.
items.body:
Wassup gang, so sorry its been a few weeks since my last email but there
was a bott load of absolutely nothing going on for a few weeks so i didnt
care to write anything lol. ANYWAYS, transfers happened. But before i get
into that... 2 days before transfers, ME AND ELDER LANGSTON PUT SOMEONE ON
DATE! it was so cool. We went to go visit her, her name is sue. Idk why but
we both clicked on her profile during daily planning and felt like he
should go see her. Since it was langstons last day with me, he made a joke
saying "were going to ask someone to be baptized today, just right on their
doorstep." Haha funny... well we went to sues house and we had a pretty
good lesson with her. This was like the 3rd time i had ever seen her and
then in my head i thought "invite her to be baptized" heck no, it was just
a funny joke langston made this morning. After the lesson we broke down the
lesson in the car and i mentioned how i thought about it AND HE DID TOO! so
we were late for a member taking us to lunch so we hurried and did that
then we went BACK to sues house and knocked on her door, langston shared
2nephi 2:2 i think and she said "i was reading that as you knocked on my
door" legit wow... then we proceeded to give her the rundown and asked her
to be baptized and we told her we really felt like its right for her in
this moment AND YOU KNOW WHAT SHE SAID "i was just thinking the same thing
as you two left my house earlier" Woah, the spirit was so strong. She then
accepted the invitation to be baptized. Wow that was crazy.
Then it was a few busy crazy days until transfers... i hate blind
transfers.... but then i got the news im going to the west side! Cool, so
we got in the van and went a few hours over there where i found out i was
going to the Bitteroot YSA area!! SO PRETTY OVER HERE! My new comp is Elder
Welch and he is an ABSOLUTE DOG! Hes such a stud and just awesome haha, hes
been out for about 18 months i think. Other big news, when he said "elder
andersen you will be eith elder welch, and you will be the Bitteroot Zone
Leaders" WHAT THE CRAP! anyways pretty cool, no idea what im doing here but
its been awesome and great and very eventful recently. Shout out to the
eppichs because i will be visiting them soon 😛 also we live with 2 other
elders now in a trailer house, pretty sick actually. One of them is known
as stinky Johnson... he lives up to it is all i will say but they are all
awesome! But super super messy. Me and welch have been cleaning the crap
out of this place. I love it here and i love you all! Thanks to the people
who sent me the most elite halloween packages and snacks! (Shoutout aunt
Kristen and the chases and the walkers🥳) keep living it up wherever you
are and ill try my darndest to do so here lol.

New address: 169 Martin St Victor, MT 59875 United States

Google photos: https://photos.app.goo.gl/1WEHmn7CFajqm1t78

items.subject: Trust
items.summary: Elder Jonas Adamson shares a torn shoulder, a birthday shout-out, and thoughts on trusting God's plan.
items.body:
Why do bad things happen to us? Why is there evil in this world? Why do we
have to feel pain?

Flics
https://photos.app.goo.gl/7bFdvqWR1mgYESD69

First off on a positive note HAPPY BIRTHDAY TO MY BOY MAX BARTON!!! What a
dawg (unc). Love you 🤞🏿

So bad news fans I am writing this from the ER. I tore my shoulder. Not
even the most tragic thing that happened this last week. Byu lost to Utah.
Hence the preceding questions.

But this has given me some time to reflect and ponder. 2 main ideas have
been on my mind lately.

How do I trust in God's Plan?

How do I better overcome adversity?

Something that I *KNOW* is that The Book of Mormon truly does provide
answers to these questions of the soul. Try it out with your own questions.

I know what God's Plan is for me. In Moses 1:39 we learn that His work and
glory is to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of us. There is
nothing greater or of higher honor than assisting our God in this work. The
Book of Mormon has a plethora of stories about missionary work. I firmly
believe that the reason I am living right now is to prepare the earth for
the Second Coming of our Lord and Savior. Serving a mission is a big part
of that. It is a Priesthood Duty. It doesn't stop with a mission too. In
business, family, sports, we should always be assisting the Father in His
work.

Now I do not know what will happen with my shoulder. It could be another
torn labrum which means surgery. It could take me out of the game for a
little. But I do know, and have complete and full confidence in, that
Nephi's words in 1 Nephi 3:7 are true. No matter what happens here with my
shoulder I know that serving a mission is my commandment. It is my work and
glory.

7 And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do
the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth
no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for
them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.

I want you to know that these words are true. The Lord will not give us
commandments unless He prepares the way to accomplish them. Expect miracles
Friends and Family. And prayers would be much appreciated.

As far as it goes for overcoming adversity, I will invite you all to listen
to Jon Hunstmans BYU devotional: God Did Not Put Us Here to Fail

There is opposition in all things. We need it that's why

Love you all
Elder Adamson
